source_act: Section 130 & 213, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 & Police Conduct Rules
user_query: A traffic police constable snatched my car keys and forced me to step out during a routine vehicle check.
legal_text_raw: Traffic police officers do NOT have the legal authority to snatch ignition keys or physically pull drivers out during routine checks. Officers below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) cannot issue compoundable traffic challans. You have the right to ask for their name, rank, and challan book/e-device.

source_act: Section 185, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended 2019)
user_query: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for drunk driving in India and what are the penalties?
legal_text_raw: The legal blood alcohol limit is 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected by a breath analyzer. Exceeding this limit under Section 185 attracts a court challan with fine up to Rs 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months for first offense, and Rs 15,000 and/or 2 years jail for repeat offense.
layman_explanation: The legal blood alcohol limit is 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected by a breath analyzer. Exceeding this limit under Section 185 attracts a court challan with fine up to Rs 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months for first offense, and Rs 15,000 and/or 2 years jail for repeat offense.

source_act: Section 206 & 207, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
user_query: Can traffic police impound my vehicle for a simple red-light jumping or speeding violation?
legal_text_raw: No. Vehicles cannot be seized for minor traffic infractions like speeding or red light jumping. Seizure under Section 207 is restricted to severe violations: driving without registration, without a valid permit, driving an overloaded commercial vehicle, or driving without insurance.
layman_explanation: No. Vehicles cannot be seized for minor traffic infractions like speeding or red light jumping. Seizure under Section 207 is restricted to severe violations: driving without registration, without a valid permit, driving an overloaded commercial vehicle, or driving without insurance.

source_act: Section 165 & 166, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
user_query: My car met with an accident due to an uninsured speeding truck. How can my family claim compensation for injuries?
legal_text_raw: You can file a claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) having territorial jurisdiction. Even if the offending vehicle is uninsured, the vehicle owner is personally liable. For hit-and-run cases, the government operates a statutory Solatium Fund providing compensation.

user_query: Do I have to carry original physical driving license, RC, and insurance documents while driving?

Traffic police cannot insist on physical copies if digital ones are shown.

source_act: Section 208 & 209, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
user_query: Can traffic police arrest me on the spot if I cannot pay the cash challan immediately?
legal_text_raw: No. Traffic violations are compoundable offenses. If you cannot pay the compound fine on the spot, the officer issues a formal notice/court challan. You have the statutory right to contest the challan or pay it online within the stipulated notice period or before the Virtual Traffic Court.

source_act: Section 134A, Motor Vehicles Act (Good Samaritan Law)
user_query: If I help a road accident victim and take them to the hospital, can the police harass me or force me to become a witness?
legal_text_raw: No. Under Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act (Good Samaritan Guidelines), any citizen who assists an accident victim is protected from civil and criminal liability, cannot be compelled to disclose identity, and hospitals cannot demand payment from the helper before initiating emergency care.
layman_explanation: No. Under Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act (Good Samaritan Guidelines), any citizen who assists an accident victim is protected from civil and criminal liability, cannot be compelled to disclose identity, and hospitals cannot demand payment from the helper before initiating emergency care.

source_act: Supreme Court & MoRTH Traffic Towing Guidelines
user_query: Can traffic police tow away a two-wheeler or car if the driver or passenger is sitting inside it?
legal_text_raw: No. Traffic police guidelines strictly prohibit towing any vehicle if a person is sitting inside it. The officer must first ask the driver to step out or pay the compound parking challan.

source_act: Section 208, Motor Vehicles Act & State Traffic Grievance Portal
user_query: What should I do if a fake automated speed camera e-challan is issued showing a different car with my number plate?
legal_text_raw: This indicates vehicle number cloning or camera OCR error. Immediately submit a grievance with photos of your actual vehicle on the state Parivahan e-Challan portal (echallan.parivahan.gov.in) to void the challan, and lodge an FIR for number plate forgery.

source_act: Section 206(4), Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety)
user_query: Can traffic police seize my driving license on the spot for talking on a mobile phone while driving?
legal_text_raw: Yes. Under Section 206(4) MV Act, police can impound and forward the driving license to the RTO for suspension of at least 3 months for specific offenses: using phone while driving, speeding, jumping red lights, and drunk driving.

source_act: Section 129, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended 2019)
user_query: Is it mandatory for a pillion rider on a two-wheeler to wear a helmet in India?
legal_text_raw: Yes. Section 129 mandates that every person above 4 years of age riding on a two-wheeler (including the pillion rider) must wear a protective headgear conforming to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) norms, with exceptions only for turban-wearing Sikhs.

source_act: Rule 115(7), Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
user_query: What is the legal validity period of a Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate for BS4 and BS6 vehicles?
legal_text_raw: For new motor vehicles, the first PUC certificate issued by the manufacturer is valid for 1 year. Thereafter, all BS4 and BS6 compliant four-wheelers must obtain PUC renewal every 12 months (or 6 months for older vehicles).
layman_explanation: For new motor vehicles, the first PUC certificate issued by the manufacturer is valid for 1 year. Thereafter, all BS4 and BS6 compliant four-wheelers must obtain PUC renewal every 12 months (or 6 months for older vehicles).

legal_text_raw: No. Traffic officers on enforcement duty must wear their official uniform with visible name badge, shoulder rank insignia, and carry an authorized electronic challan terminal or challan book. A plainclothes officer cannot issue on-the-spot traffic fines.

source_act: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 & Municipal Corporation Bylaws
user_query: Can a private parking lot operator put a wheel-clamp on my vehicle and demand Rs 1,000 fine for parking beyond time?
legal_text_raw: Private commercial malls or parking contractors have no statutory penal authority to levy arbitrary fines or clamp wheels without municipal authorization. They can only charge reasonable parking fees. Forcible wheel clamping amounts to wrongful restraint under Section 126 BNS.

user_query: Can an insurance company reject a motor accident claim because the driver was carrying an expired driving license?
legal_text_raw: While driving with an expired license is an offense, insurance companies cannot automatically reject third-party claims unless the absence of license contributed directly to the accident. For own damage claims, grace periods and renewal rules apply.

legal_text_raw: Yes. If a breath analyzer indicates or a police officer has reasonable cause to suspect drug or alcohol impairment, the officer can require the driver to provide a specimen of breath, blood, or urine at a registered hospital under medical supervision.

source_act: Section 4, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
user_query: What is the minimum age to obtain a Learner's License for a gearless scooter in India?
legal_text_raw: The minimum age for driving a motorcycle without gear (up to 50cc engine capacity) with parental consent is 16 years. For all other motor vehicles, the minimum legal age is strictly 18 years.
layman_explanation: The minimum age for driving a motorcycle without gear (up to 50cc engine capacity) with parental consent is 16 years. For all other motor vehicles, the minimum legal age is strictly 18 years.

source_act: Section 199A, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended 2019)
user_query: Can an owner be prosecuted if they allow an underage minor child to drive their car or scooter?
legal_text_raw: Yes. Under Section 199A, the parent or vehicle owner is held criminally liable, facing up to 3 years imprisonment and Rs 25,000 fine. The vehicle registration is canceled for 1 year, and the juvenile cannot obtain a license until age 25.
layman_explanation: Yes. Under Section 199A, the parent or vehicle owner is held criminally liable, facing up to 3 years imprisonment and Rs 25,000 fine. The vehicle registration is canceled for 1 year, and the juvenile cannot obtain a license until age 25.

source_act: Avishek Goenka v. Union of India (Supreme Court, 2012)
user_query: Is sun control window tint film completely banned on cars in India?
legal_text_raw: Yes. The Supreme Court banned the use of any black film or pasted tint film on vehicle glass. Front and rear windscreens must have at least 70% Visual Light Transmission (VLT), and side windows at least 50% VLT, provided solely by the glass manufacturer.
layman_explanation: Yes. The Supreme Court banned the use of any black film or pasted tint film on vehicle glass. Front and rear windscreens must have at least 70% Visual Light Transmission (VLT), and side windows at least 50% VLT, provided solely by the glass manufacturer.

layman_explanation: Yes, provided the transport/commercial vehicle's unladen weight does not exceed 7,500 kg (Light Motor Vehicle). A separate commercial transport endorsement is not required for driving an LMV taxi.

source_act: Section 50, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
user_query: Can a buyer be held liable for traffic challans incurred by the seller before the vehicle was sold?
legal_text_raw: Traffic challans attach to the registered vehicle and owner at the time of the violation. The buyer can produce the dated Sale Agreement and delivery receipt to establish non-liability for pre-sale traffic violations.
